issues.description: Constructor mismatch for Bookstore.init: The problem statement requires a constructor with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). The solution implementation defines init() with no parameters and uses an undefined identifier 'books' inside its body (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift in the solution, initializer at lines 14-16). This contradicts the expected constructor and causes a compile error when Client attempts to construct a Bookstore using Bookstore(books: books) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift in the solution, line 57). The template file currently contains only task comments and no implementation (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift in the template, lines 3-16), so it must be updated to provide the correct initializer signature as well.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Bookstore initializer to match the problem statement: implement init(books: [Book]) and assign self.books = books. Update the solution and the template Bookstore.swift files so the initializer signature is `init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }`. Ensure Client code that constructs Bookstore(books: books) will compile against this correct initializer.

issues.description: The concept is the Bookstore initializer (constructor) used to create a Bookstore with an initial collection of books. The problem statement explicitly requires an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). The Client code constructs a Bookstore using Bookstore(books: books) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift line 57). However, the Solution implementation of the Bookstore class defines init() with no parameters (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 14-16). This mismatch of constructor signatures means students cannot directly map the required initializer from the problem to the provided implementation and the example call in Client; it also leads to compilation errors or confusion about which initializer to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift match the problem statement and call site. Replace the no-argument init() with init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books } so that Client(books: books) compiles and the required constructor is consistent across artifacts.
